correctness.rationale: For A=-aI+bJ, the backward-Euler multiplier has squared Euclidean norm f(t)=(1+2at+(a²+b²)t²)^{-1}. A direct factor identity proves the claimed globally supporting tangent line, and f is convex after its tangency point. Jensen over the resulting convex minorant gives the sharp bound for every Borel step law, with strict equality conditions proving unique attainment/nonattainment. Symbolic identities and exact rational values replayed in verify.py; the numerical checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The first sharp criterion for when fixed-mean step randomization can improve squared-norm damping in a natural damped normal mode, coupled with a complete optimizer and a strict-positive/nonattainment distinction, supplies a motivated structural benchmark for randomized implicit integration. The exact boundary b²=3a² separates the convex and nonconvex response regimes. The result is not presented as a convergence-rate or solver-speed improvement.
